title: Bounded monthly ranks kept a negative six-month Nino 3.4 change statistic in ERSSTv5 for 1950-2025
abstract: We tested whether a prior six-month Nino 3.4 cooling imbalance depends on large temperature values. We removed month means and a linear trend from a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 record for 1950-2025. We replaced residual values by bounded uniform ranks within each calendar month. The normalized third moment of six-month changes was -0.453, with a conditional 95% five-year block interval of -0.760 to -0.100. Pooled uniform and normal ranks also gave negative intervals. Thus the cubic imbalance remained when original temperature spacings and monthly value distributions were removed. Excluding all pairs that touched 1982-1983, 1997-1998 or 2015-2016 gave -0.273, with an interval of -0.580 to 0.080. The early-era interval also included zero. These checks limit claims of a stable effect. The study extends earlier tests of the same record; it is not an independent replication. Ranks, fitted terms and source errors are not resampled. Short records, seasonal dynamics, prior selection and conditional intervals limit inference. No physical cause or event duration is identified. Code, annual aggregate evidence, uncertainty draws, an independent arithmetic check and source hashes support reproduction.

display.caption: Six-month change statistics before and after rank transforms, with conditional 95% five-year block intervals. Right: monthly ranks in two eras and after joint endpoint exclusions. The early-era and joint-exclusion intervals include zero.

Prior stationary surrogate test motivates a check without original temperature spacings.
Prior seasonal surrogate test left extreme-event leverage open. We test bounded ranks and endpoint exclusions, not a new surrogate model.
